title: 09. Backend Python: REST API DESIGN BEST PRACTICES
summary: REST API DESIGN BEST PRACTICES: URL NAMING CONVENTIONS  GOOD: GET /users → List users GET /users/123 → Get user 123 POST /users → Create user PUT /users/123…; REST API DESIGN — Interview Must-Know.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```python name=api_design/rest_best_practices.py
# ============================================================
# REST API DESIGN — Interview Must-Know
# ============================================================

"""
1. URL NAMING CONVENTIONS
========================
✅ GOOD:
  GET    /users              → List users
  GET    /users/123          → Get user 123
  POST   /users              → Create user
  PUT    /users/123          → Full update user 123
  PATCH  /users/123          → Partial update user 123
  DELETE /users/123          → Delete user 123
  GET    /users/123/orders   → Get orders for user 123

❌ BAD:
  GET    /getUsers
  POST   /createUser
  GET    /user/delete/123
  POST   /users/123/update

Rules:
  - Use NOUNS, not verbs (HTTP method IS the verb)
  - Use PLURAL nouns (/users not /user)
  - Use KEBAB-CASE for multi-word (/order-items not /orderItems)
  - Use QUERY PARAMS for filtering: /users?role=admin&active=true
  - Use PATH PARAMS for identity: /users/123
  - Nest for relationships: /users/123/orders

2. HTTP STATUS CODES
====================
  200 OK              → Successful GET/PUT/PATCH
  201 Created         → Successful POST (resource created)
  204 No Content      → Successful DELETE (no body)
  400 Bad Request     → Client sent invalid data
  401 Unauthorized    → Not authenticated (no/invalid token)
  403 Forbidden       → Authenticated but not authorized
  404 Not Found       → Resource doesn't exist
  409 Conflict        → Duplicate resource (email already exists)
  422 Unprocessable   → Validation error (FastAPI default)
  429 Too Many Reqs   → Rate limited
  500 Internal Error  → Server bug

3. RESPONSE FORMAT
==================
{
    "data": { ... },          // or list for collections
    "meta": {
        "page": 1,
        "page_size": 10,
        "total": 100,
        "total_pages": 10
    },
    "errors": null
}

Error format:
{
    "errors": [
        {
            "field": "email",
            "message": "Invalid email format",
            "code": "INVALID_EMAIL"
        }
    ]
}

4. PAGINATION
=============
  /users?page=2&page_size=20        → Offset-based
  /users?cursor=abc123&limit=20     → Cursor-based (better for large datasets)

5. VERSIONING
=============
  /api/v1/users      → URL versioning (most common)
  Accept: application/vnd.api.v1+json  → Header versioning

6. IDEMPOTENCY
==============
  GET    → Always idempotent (same result every time)
  PUT    → Idempotent (same update = same result)
  DELETE → Idempotent (deleting already-deleted = still gone)
  POST   → NOT idempotent (creates new resource each time)
  PATCH  → May or may not be idempotent
"""
```
